title: Mount Keen from Glen Esk
listingBlurb: Long Glen Esk walk-in, steady climb, big plateau top — full day, no traced line on here.
summary: Classic Keen from Invermark: long walk in, steady up, open plateau and summit. Straightforward in clear weather, still a big day. No polyline or GPX — map’s centred on the glen for context, not a drawn path.
parkingNote: Invermark / Glen Esk — access, gates, and parking change with signs and season. Read them. Don’t block passing places or working tracks. Long walk in from there; still no traced line on this site.

disclaimerSection.title: No line on this page
disclaimerSection.body: No polyline, GPX, or waypoint list here — you get parker, rough shape, terrain, and usual feel. Where you walk is your map, the ground, and a proper mountain forecast. Bring both and use them.

weatherNote.title: Before you go
weatherNote.body: Mountain forecast for where you’ll actually walk, not just the town. You want a decent window — long day, plateau catches wind.
weatherNote.supporting: This page doesn’t update — check live conditions.

whyThisRoute.title: Why pick this day?
whyThisRoute.body: When you want a full Glen Esk day — legs, headspace, summit that feels earned. Long walk in, climb, big top. Needs time and a half-decent forecast, not a two-hour dash.
callouts: Steady rhythm once you’re going — fine for a head-clear.
Broad top and plateau — big sky, not a ridge puzzle.
whyThisRoute.supporting: Wind, clag, or winter still make it serious — distance hurts. Bailing early is smart, not a failure.

recommendationBlock.title: Rough take
lines: Pack for a big day: food, water, and when it gets dark — especially off-summer.
Great headspace walk if the forecast’s sound; grim if you’re chasing sunset or pretending it’ll be fine.
recommendationBlock.supporting: Shape’s simple — long in, up, out — but line and bail points are still yours.

qualityMeter.headline: A full Glen Esk day with a steady pulse
qualityMeter.verdict: Grand when the weather plays ball; a grind when it doesn’t.

factors.label: Day length
factors.note: Bigger than a half-day poke — plan like you mean it.

factors.label: Summit character
factors.note: Broad, open top — room to breathe if visibility’s decent.

factors.label: Weather exposure
factors.note: Plateau and height catch wind and clag like anywhere else.

factors.label: No traced line on this page
factors.note: We’re not drawing your line — that’s you and the map.

whatDayFeelsLike.title: What it feels like
whatDayFeelsLike.body: Long settle along the glen, then steady pull onto open ground. Day stretches — not frantic, just keeps going. Good day: quiet, a bit meditative. Rough day: miles and weather.
whatDayFeelsLike.supporting: Legs know about it by the finish. Have a bail story before you need it.
summaryLines: Long approach, steady climb, broad summit feel.
Headspace day if you’ve got the window for it.

terrainDetail.title: Terrain & vibe
terrainDetail.body: Track and path low down, then usual Scottish mix — heather, grass, wet bits, open higher up. Nothing fancy; distance and height stack up. Winter: ice, snow, short days; same respect as any Munro.
terrainDetail.supporting: Estate tracks and signs — stick to what’s allowed.

goodStopsDetail.intro: Break spots that usually work — not waypoints, just habit.

spots.title: Before the climb bites
spots.description: If you’re already rushed or low on water, fix that in the glen — not halfway up when you’re committed.

spots.title: Somewhere out of the worst wind
spots.description: On open ground, a slight lee or dip beats lunch on the highest exposed lump.

anchorRefsIntro: Labels for chat and map checks — not a sequence to march.
notes: Suits a decent weather window and a bigger day — not a mad dash after a late lunch without checking light.
Access, gates, and parking change — read signs.
Maps link uses the centre near Invermark / the glen — check against your own map before you drive.
